clue.text: Exchange lies concealing source of investment

indicators.note: the words Exchange lies keep the answer tucked away across the join between them

explanation.surface: A market trader's lies are hiding where the money really comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' looks like a stock exchange or a verb, but it simply supplies letters to a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre and start-up slang, a wealthy private backer who puts money into a venture is called this.

clue.text: Letter opener chopped up dead seers

indicators.note: chopped up suggests the letters of dead seers cut into pieces and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A paperknife has been used to hack up some deceased prophets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter opener' looks like a paperknife, which fits 'chopped up'; it is the person who opens a letter sent to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The recipient a letter is directed to is the one who opens it, a witty paraphrase.

clue.text: Serious head of governing party

indicators.note: head of points to the opening letter of the word governing

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A description of the solemn leader of the ruling political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' reads as a political party but is a dance party, RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something solemn or weighty in manner or consequence.

clue.text: Stockholders step back after French article

indicators.note: after places the reversed step behind the French article in the answer

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a step is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a stair is a single step

explanation.surface: Shareholders retreat after reading something in a French newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stockholders' suggests investors, but the stock here is cattle, held by cowboys' ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassos are ropes used by cowboys to catch and hold cattle, that is, livestock, so they are holders of stock.

clue.text: Curtains separate around hazard

parts.note: curtains is slang for the end, or death

indicators.note: around signals that the word for separate is turned round

parts.note: to part is to separate

explanation.surface: Drapes hanging apart around something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' looks like drapes, but is slang for the end of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous place or structure likely to cause fatal accidents is a serious hazard.

clue.text: Condemned like St Paul's with hole in

indicators.note: in shows the hole letter set inside the word for having a dome

parts.note: St Paul's Cathedral in London has a famous dome, so it is domed
O is a round hole by its shape

explanation.surface: A cathedral found to have a hole in it is declared beyond saving.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul's is the domed cathedral in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sentenced to a dreadful fate, or fated to fail, is condemned to it.

clue.text: Came to a vigil with Scottish hooligan

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept beside a dead body
ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: Someone attended an all-night watch accompanied by a Glasgow tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: NED is Scottish slang for a young thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, which is to be roused from sleep or a faint.

clue.text: Crop top with footless deer on front

indicators.note: on front puts the shortened deer before the garment
footless means the bottom letter of the deer word is cut off

parts.note: a hart is a male red deer
a vest is an upper-body garment, a top

explanation.surface: A cropped top printed with a deer missing its feet on the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop top' reads as a garment; 'Crop' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gathering of a season's crop, or the crop itself, is this word.

clue.text: Headless spirit in peril

indicators.note: headless means the leading letter of the word for spirit is removed

parts.note: friskiness is playful liveliness or spirit

explanation.surface: A ghost with no head is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost, which fits 'Headless'; it means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being dangerous or hazardous amounts to peril.

clue.text: Criticises suppressing good for fast results

indicators.note: suppressing suggests the criticism holding down the good letter inside it

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A critic who stifles anything good to get rapid results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means going without food, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without food brings sharp hunger aches, so these are what fasting produces.

clue.text: Hear radio broadcast complaint

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of hear radio are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to listen to a radio programme of grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a complaint is an illness, and this bowel disorder is one.

clue.text: Restored from death, Romeo lives with nurse

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
is means exists or lives
EN is an Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: Romeo comes back to life, dwelling with Juliet's Nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Romeo and Juliet, where the Nurse is a character.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brought back to life after dying has risen, as in the Easter story.

clue.text: Promote cheer around centre of Montevideo

indicators.note: around shows the word for cheer wrapping the central letters

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or make happy

indicators.note: centre of takes the two middle letters of Montevideo

explanation.surface: Boost morale throughout the heart of the Uruguayan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to a higher rank is to promote them.

clue.text: European soldiers returning to mid-east oddly missing adversaries …

indicators.note: returning tells us the soldiers word is read back to front

parts.note: men are soldiers, especially rank and file

indicators.note: oddly missing means the odd-numbered letters of mid-east are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: European troops heading back to the Middle East, where foes await.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes NEM from MEN; the even letters of 'mid-east' give IES.
explanation.definitionFit: Foes or opponents are those who stand against you.

clue.text: … scattered over housing section

indicators.note: housing means the spare word holds the section letter within it

parts.note: spare means left over, surplus

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: enemies spread out over a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like dwellings but means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly spread, with gaps between, describes something scattered.

clue.text: Elysium possibly back Queen biography

parts.note: aft means at the back of a ship
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a life is a biography, as in a life of Johnson

explanation.surface: A possible paradise is found in the back of a royal biography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks Elysium as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium is the Greek paradise of the blessed dead, one example of existence after dying.

clue.text: Struggles, missing wife, to get son on the move

indicators.note: missing tells us the wife letter is absent from the struggles word

parts.note: wrestles means struggles or grapples

explanation.surface: A man fights on alone without his wife to get his son moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to keep still is always moving and fidgeting.

clue.text: Celebrity in court following second disorderly arrest

indicators.note: following puts the court word after the second letter

parts.note: a defendant up before the judge is up, or in court

indicators.note: disorderly signals the letters of arrest are jumbled

explanation.surface: A famous person ends up in court after an arrest for disorderly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' looks like part of a charge but rearranges ARREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely famous star or celebrity, especially in entertainment or sport.

clue.text: Unstable new currency gets nervous reaction

parts.note: the euro is the European currency
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A shaky new currency makes the markets twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious and emotionally unsteady is described as mentally unstable.

clue.text: Things bird found in receding river

indicators.note: found in places the bird inside the reversed river
receding means going backwards, so the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Objects a bird discovered as the river's floodwaters went down.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate existing items or beings are things.

clue.text: Exchange upcoming missile with a German

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a dart is a small thrown missile
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Swapping a soon-to-launch missile with a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing over an old item as part payment for a new one is a part-exchange deal.

clue.text: Foul setter on ship getting high

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to themself as me
SS is steamship
up means high, raised

explanation.surface: The setter, on board a ship, gets an unpleasant high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to botch.
explanation.definitionFit: To foul something up is to bungle or spoil it.

clue.text: Bits of corn on baking range one hears

parts.note: ears are the grain-bearing heads of corn
baking means extremely hot, as in weather

explanation.surface: Pieces of corn being cooked on a kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a cooker, fitting 'baking', but is a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance within which sounds can be heard is this hearing range.

clue.text: Rotten guide is not quite right

parts.note: food gone bad is off
a key is a guide, as to a map or code

explanation.surface: A useless guidebook that is a little inaccurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Music slightly out of tune, or anything somewhat amiss or inappropriate, is described so.

clue.text: Way beneficiary reported brigand

indicators.note: reported means the two words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: a course is a way or route; an heir is a beneficiary of a will

explanation.surface: A will's beneficiary turns out, by the way, to be a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: COURSE + HEIR spoken together sounds like the pirate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate, a sea-going robber or bandit.

clue.text: Tightly embrace object of desire

definitions.meaning: to squeeze someone hard in a hug
the person one is infatuated with

explanation.surface: Hugging hard the person you are longing for.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means squeeze hard; the noun is a passing infatuation or its target.

clue.text: Always showing excitement about gold

indicators.note: about means the excitement word goes round the gold

parts.note: fever is a state of nervous excitement
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone who perpetually gets excited about gold.
explanation.definitionFit: For all time, eternally, is the sense of always.

clue.text: Six aluminium and sulphur containers

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Six vessels holding aluminium and sulphur in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass bottles for liquids or medicine are a kind of container.

clue.text: Bond starts to uncover nefarious international terrorist enterprise

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letter of each of the five following words

explanation.surface: James Bond sets out to expose a sinister global terror plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007 but is the verb, to join.
explanation.definitionFit: To join together or fasten is to bond things.

clue.text: Spooner's fish dish is to be encouraged

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after Reverend Spooner

parts.note: hake is a fish of the cod family
a tart is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A fish dish seems to inspire confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of HAKE TART gives TAKE HART, spelt as the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain courage or confidence is the idiomatic sense of being encouraged.

clue.text: Distribute handy cure for disorder

indicators.note: distribute means hand round, so the letters of handy cure are spread out anew

explanation.surface: Instructions to dispense a convenient remedy for an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' reads as an ailment, fitting 'cure', but means uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outcry or commotion, originally the shout raised to pursue a criminal, is a clamour.

clue.text: Weapon was re-examined having backfired

indicators.note: having backfired means the exam word is turned back to front

parts.note: resat means took an exam again

explanation.surface: A weapon was checked again after it misfired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfired' suggests a gun but reverses RESAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun firing electrified darts is a modern police weapon.
